title: Tenant SLO Migration: Safe Drain and Eviction Procedure
author: Elena Morozova
content:
Overview:
This runbook describes the safe, observable procedure for migrating tenant SLO contracts between backend pools and performing controlled tenant drain/eviction when required. It covers preconditions, capacity hedging, error-budget handoffs, automated tooling, canary steps, rollback criteria, and post-migration incident review standards. Intended audience: SRE oncall, platform engineers, and solutions engineers executing tenant migrations or emergency evictions.

Why this exists:
- Migrations and controlled evictions are high-risk operations: they impact SLOs, customer experience, and billing.
- We must preserve SLO commitments (latency and availability) while ensuring fair capacity distribution across tenants.
- This runbook codifies operational policy to minimize surprises and enable rapid, evidence-driven postmortems.

Key definitions and SLO expectations:
- Tenant SLO Contract: a tuple of availability SLO, latency SLO (p50/p95/p99), and any throughput or SLA clauses (e.g., burst allowances).
- Default migration safety thresholds: availability >= 99.95% (30d), p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive endpoints, error budget consumption <= 30% in last 7d prior to migration.
- Hedging capacity: temporary excess capacity allocated to the target pool to absorb migration bursts (recommended 10–25% of migrating tenant's peak RPS).

Pre-migration checklist (must be completed before starting):
1) Ownership and approvals:
   - Confirm migration owner (platform engineer) and secondary oncall.
   - Confirm business owner approval for any scheduled evictions.
2) SLO and error budget validation:
   - Verify tenant error budget consumption: should be <= 30% over last 7d. If >30%, raise to "migration with caution" state and require senior SRE signoff.
   - Confirm SLO contract version tags for source and target pools.
3) Capacity and routing readiness:
   - Ensure target pool has hedging capacity: target_pool.available_gpu_slots >= migrating_peak_rps * hedging_multiplier (default 1.15).
   - Validate autoscaler cooldowns and burst policies are tuned for migration window.
4) Telemetry and alerting:
   - Create temporary synthetic canaries for the tenant (3 endpoints, 1rps each) and configure dashboard with p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate.
   - Ensure alert thresholds are active: p95 > 400ms or availability drop > 0.1% triggers immediate rollback.
5) Rollback plan and comms:
   - Document rollback steps, required IAM principals, CLI commands, and expected timeline (target < 10 minutes to rollback full traffic).
   - Notify stakeholders and set status in #platform-ops and incident channel.

Automated tooling and commands (examples):
- Dry-run migration plan (shows capacity delta and routing plan):
  $ rlctl migration plan --tenant my-tenant --from pool-a --to pool-b --dry-run

- Start phased drain (phase size = 10% by default):
  $ rlctl migration start --tenant my-tenant --to pool-b --phase-size 10 --monitor true

- Force immediate rollback:
  $ rlctl migration rollback --tenant my-tenant --to pool-a --force --reason "p95 spike"

Phased migration procedure (recommended):
1) Phase 0 (Canary verification):
   - Route 1% of traffic (or 10 RPS, whichever smaller) to the target pool.
   - Observe telemetry for 15 minutes. Key checks: p95, error rate, queue backlog, model KV miss rate.
   - Pass criteria: no p95 spike > 2x baseline, error rate <= baseline + 0.05%.
2) Phase 1..N (gradual ramp):
   - Increase routed traffic in increments of 10% with a 10–15 minute observation window per phase.
   - If any threshold breach occurs, pause and investigate; consider 5% rollback if effect is localized.
3) Finalization:
   - After 100% traffic is shifted and stable for 30 minutes, mark migration complete and remove temporary canaries.

Emergency eviction procedure (when tenant is exceeding safety thresholds or causing cross-tenant degradation):
1) Trigger criteria (any of):
   - Tenant consumes > 60% of cluster memory/GPU for > 10 minutes and is not throttled by quotas.
   - Tenant error budget consumption => 100% within 24h and causing repeated retries/fallbacks across hosts.
   - Tenant-caused degradation returns cross-tenant p95 increases > 15% on core services.
2) Eviction steps (fast path):
   - Notify stakeholders and set channel status.
   - Quarantine new admissions: update ingress policy to return 429 for non-admin control-plane clients.
   - Begin eviction: $ rlctl tenant evict --tenant my-tenant --mode graceful --grace-period 120
   - If graceful eviction fails to reduce load within 5 minutes, escalate to force eviction: $ rlctl tenant evict --tenant my-tenant --mode force
3) Post-eviction diagnostics:
   - Collect per-host logs, kernel metrics, GPU utilization, and scheduler decisions for the 30 minutes preceding eviction.
   - Capture model runtime stack traces and KV cache eviction stats.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback triggers):
- p95 latency on target pool > 3x baseline for > 5 minutes.
- Availability drop > 0.25% absolute across tenant or >0.1% across aggregate customer-facing endpoints.
- Error rate spikes > 0.5% absolute from baseline.
- Sudden increase in queue depth or persistent GC/OOM signals on target hosts.

SLO-awareness in incident review and postmortem standards:
- Any migration or eviction that resulted in SLO breaches requires a structured incident review with the following minimum evidence: migration plan, telemetry dashboards, rlctl logs, alert timeline, and mitigation actions.
- Postmortem must include: root cause hypothesis, detection latency, error-budget delta, capacity delta, an action owner for each remediation item, and a follow-up timeline (max 30 days).
- Severity determination: if customer-facing availability drops > 0.5% or >3 tenants impacted for > 30 minutes, classify as Sev2 and notify executive oncall.

Capacity planning and debt mitigation guidance:
- Maintain a "migration buffer" of 15% available capacity in each region for scheduled tenant migrations.
- For long-running draining of large tenants (> 2k RPS), schedule during low-traffic windows and pre-warm target pools (warm replicas, primed KV caches).
- Track migration-related capacity debt in the SRE backlog and prioritize optimizations that reduce cache cold-starts and first-token latency.

Telemetry and dashboards to monitor during operations:
- Tenant migration dashboard (default panels): routed-traffic %, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, request queue depth, KV cache hit rate, host GPU utilization, autoscaler actions, ingress rejects (429s).
- Alerting matrix (examples):
  | Signal | Threshold | Action |
  |--------|-----------|--------|
  | p95 latency | > 400ms (tenant) | Pause migration, investigate model runtime |
  | Error rate | > baseline + 0.5% | Rollback 10% traffic, open incident |
  | Host GPU load | > 90% sustained 5m | Add temporary capacity, migrate other low-priority tenants |
Operational responsibilities and ownership:
- Migration owner: executes runbook and holds the migration lock until finalization.
- Oncall SRE: monitoring, immediate rollback authority if thresholds breach.
- Platform engineering: responsible for rlctl automation and capacity provisioning.
- Solutions engineering: communicates customer impacts and billing reconciliations.

After-action and continuous improvement:
1) Immediate (within 24h): create incident record and collect required evidence.
2) Short-term (within 7d): perform blameless postmortem, identify 3 concrete mitigations (automation, telemetry, capacity).
3) Long-term (30d): schedule follow-up work into SRE roadmap; update migration automation if it required manual intervention.

Appendix A — Example migration YAML (used by rlctl):
---
migration_request:
  tenant: "my-tenant"
  from_pool: "pool-a"
  to_pool: "pool-b"
  phase_size_percent: 10
  canary_rps: 5
  hedging_multiplier: 1.15
  max_rollout_minutes: 180
  rollback_on:
    p95_multiplier: 3.0
    availability_drop_absolute: 0.0025
    error_rate_absolute: 0.005
---

Appendix B — Quick checklist (one-page) to paste in incident channel:
- Migration owner and backup named
- SLO check: last 7d error budget <= 30%
- Hedging capacity validated (>= 1.15x)
- Canary endpoints created and verified
- Alerts active for p95, error rate, host load
- Rollback CLI tested and ready
